context: Play a fixed 5×5 Minesweeper board. Cells are numbered 0 to 24 in row-major order (row = index // 5, column = index % 5). The opening at cell (0,0) is revealed first, and the standard flood-fill through zero-adjacent cells leaves exactly these cells covered: 3, 4, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19, 22, 23, 24. There are exactly four mines, all among those covered cells. The visible clues around the opening imply that each of these sets of covered neighbours contains exactly one mine: [3,8], [3,8,13], [8,13,17,18], [17], [17,22]. The supplied order is a permutation of the 12 covered indices; play the game by revealing cells in that order. Any cell already revealed by flood-fill is skipped. The game stops as soon as a mine is revealed (status 'lost') or as soon as all 21 non-mine cells are revealed (status 'won'). The returned history lists only the explicit reveals as {row, col} pairs in the order they were made, stopping at the terminal reveal. The game_id is an arbitrary identifier chosen for the game.
